Ultimately, this study contributes to a clearer picture of low-mass stellar characteristics.

A new type of fully integrated optical antenna is proposed, featuring a graphene pattern situated on both sides of a plasmonic waveguide. An analysis of line waves within this structure has been conducted using a co-propagating model, with a simulation of the graphene pattern's effect on the waves performed through COMSOL Multiphysics. The results indicate that the graphene pattern can effectively control and direct the line waves, offering enhanced design flexibility for integrated optical antennas.

We extend previous research on self-joins within the context of query evaluation, addressing its limitations by characterizing the scenario where self-joins can be used effectively. Our research builds upon prior work that established conditions for self-joins' suitability and demonstrated enhancement techniques for queries that exceed these conditions. Building on these foundations, our research addresses situations where queries contain self-joins and establish a clear distinction between query classes that admit polynomial-time and exponential-time assessment. Our primary condition for evaluating queries with conjunctive queries and integer arithmetic compares with earlier findings on foculars and schema-focused evaluations, whereas our more stringent condition includes databases of size $n^k$ that may exhibit varying densities. This condition for polynomial-time assessability allows self-joins in inequalities (strict or non-strict) within queries. Our research expands these findings to include divisible integer arithmetic assessments for such inequalities.

We investigate the continuity of rational functions over multiple valued fields, denoted as R/c, using automata theory. Building on previous work that placed the decision problem for continuity in the complexity class ALC^0, we define two corresponding problems: Continuity over valued fields (CVF) and the real-valued variant (CVR). For single-valued fields, we show that CVU is contained within the elementary elementary uniform language class EULE_0, a subset of P, and that both CVR and its non-rationality counterpart (CQR) are located within EULE_0.

This note highlights key features of the neutrino factory, particularly in relation to precision muon polarization and its significance for reducing the neutrino oscillation measurement uncertainty. The required polarization levels, around 20-30 percent, are feasible given the available polarization percentages for a 5 GeV beam and feasible polarization transfer methods. Without beam polarization, the neutrino factory would lose its unique capabilities, notably in controlling the neutrino helicity, which is critical for studying neutrino mixing angles and searching for CP violation in neutral D mesons. Furthermore, the note explores the possibility of measuring the polarization fraction in B^0 and B^0_s decays to dimuon final states via b quark semileptonic decays. Considering final states like B^0\ -> D^{*}l^{+}l^{-} and B^0_s\ -> \phi l^{+}l^{-}, we estimate the polarization fraction ratio between B^0 and B^0_s to be around 0.6-0.7, offering a notable difference in final state muon polarization. Considering final states containing a charged lepton only, we find that beam polarization would induce a around 10-20\ percent difference in forwardbackward asymmetry in l charge between B^0 and B^0_s decays due to a larger difference in the corresponding polarization fraction ratio (\sim 1.3) and thus in final state muon polarization.

This study investigates the predictive capabilities of reservoir computing for complex systems characterized by multiple co-existing dynamical states and disparate time scales. A case is examined using a chemical reaction known as Belousov-Zhabotinsky (BZ), which exhibits both fast oscillatory behavior and slow transient dynamics. It is found that standard reservoir computers struggle to accurately model this system due to the linear nature of their training algorithms. To address this challenge, we explore the effects of a non-standard error metric on RC performance. By modifying the cost function to account for both fast and slow dynamics, we are able to significantly improve the system model's accuracy. This enhanced model captures the fast limit cycles, slow trajectories, and even the quasi-periodic dynamics observed in the BZ system.

A key limitation of bias-reduced estimation techniques developed for Ising models is the unintentional introduction of smoothness, which hamples their practical application. This issue arises in methods by Sasaki and Yamanaka, which involve the use of an integral, as well as in other approaches utilizing the cumulant generating function. We present a novel approach to developing smooth, bias-reduced estimators for functions that are analytically expressible through finite sums of products of integer variables. Our method does not rely on integral-based expressions and is specifically tailored to address expression (6). This estimator is also capable of reducing the bias in solutions to equations, including those used to determine marginal probabilities and the logit function. Notably, all proposed smooth bias-reduced estimators exhibit a rate of asymptotic consistency comparable to their counterparts.

This study examines how reachable states can be determined within a specific time frame under feedback control in discrete-time switched linear systems that operate in different modes. To begin with, we model the set of states that can be reached within this time limit as the union of convex polytopes, with each polytope corresponding to a specific switching pattern. Next, we propose using over-approximation via parallel parallelpipeds to efficiently calculate these reachable states. Furthermore, we demonstrate the computation of states that remain outside a forbidden set, given a particular switching pattern and feedback control. This involves calculating states that stay within a convex polytope for an extended duration. To effectively handle this computation, we first solve the states-out-of-a-set problem for a limited time span, and then iteratively extend it to cover more prolonged time frames.

A local-functional representation (LFR) was developed as a way to effectively capture the characteristics of low-dimensional signals within a functional space.
This approach enables flexible modeling of diverse signal types while maintaining a compact, local-based framework.
Initially devised to represent and analyze biomedical time-series under a Euclidean norm, we have now generalized the theoretical basis of the LFR to accommodate non-Euclidean distances, thus allowing a broader range of signals to be efficiently described using this framework.
We have also explored various practical applications of the LFR, including signal denoising, feature extraction, support vector machines, and regression models.
We have implemented several of these applications in an open-source Python package, matlarm, for ease of use.
Here, we focus particularly on a theoretical advantage of the LFR - its ability to achieve superior generalization even with limited data due to its inherently compact nature.

For thousands of years humans have been exploiting and influencing the
animacy of natural resources, with consequences that are still felt today.
Although modern technology has significantly accelerated these effects,
fundamental questions regarding the origins, development, and nature of
humans' perceptions of and interactions with animacy remain largely
unanswered. To begin to address these questions from a contemporary
perspective, we first operationally define the continuum of animacy and then
break it down into two core components - visual categorizability and agency.
Using these components we then examine how animacy is perceived across a
continuum using both self-reported and physiological measures. Our results
indicate that agency and visual categorizability independently contribute to
perceptions of and interactions with animacy. These findings serve as an
important starting point for interdisciplinary research that can inform the
development of more sustainable and ethically aware approaches to addressing
the animacy continuum from both a human-centered and ecologically conscious
standpoint.

The continued study of automorphic L-function zeros has significant implications, affecting our comprehension of the L-function in its critical range, the zero-lies-in-the-half-plane question, the zero-cluster size at s=0, and the zero-density. This paper takes a different approach by examining the zero-cluster behavior from a combined zero-set perspective, offering a more user-friendly understanding of the "repulsion of zeros" phenomenon that is often described using intricate probability distributions from random matrix theory. To illustrate the idea of zero-cluster repulsion more clearly, the author provides three straightforward lemmas that demonstrate the non-repetition of zeros for L-functions within broader families, the exclusion of zeros within broader L-function families within specified time ranges, and the absence of overlapping zeros for L-functions within specific families with defined conductor and zero-order ranges. This paper's content can be seen as a supplementary guide to the main theorems discussed in related works such as "The Heat Equation Method for Landau-Siegel Zeros" (Compos. Math. 154, 2018), "The Heat Equation Method for the Zero-Rho Conjecture" (arXiv:1802.09988), and "Heat Kernels, Zero Repulsion, and the Distribution of Primes" (arXiv:1810.01860).

A key challenge in specifying and verifying quantum algorithms is establishing precise input-output connections. To address this, a comprehensible form of quantum relational Hoare logic has been developed, allowing for the quantitative measurement of input-output correlations through an extension to pre- and post-conditions. This logic incorporates all operations from the standard quantum instruction set and comes with a rigorous mathematical foundation, based on operations in Dirac notation that support both complete axiomatic reasoning and a fully working proof system. Furthermore, an automated tool based on this framework enables the efficient analysis of relational properties for complex programs involving nested commands and data structures like queues and recursive functions.

The Spreading-Epidemic Model (MEM) is introduced to account for high infection rate events where a single individual can rapidly infect many others within an enclosed space. Unlike standard epidemiological models, super-spreader events can increase infection rates exponentially as shown in the MEM. The effectiveness of various non-pharmaceutical interventions against the spread of such events is evaluated in the MEM. Additionally, a variant of the model incorporates spatial distribution and the spread of information about disease symptoms, showing that targeted vaccination can contain the infection but also has a drawback of promoting the spread of misinformation. The probability of a vaccine being safe but appearing symptomatic in the model can be quantified, and it is shown that even a small increase in infection rates from one infected person to multiple others can cause misinformation to spread more rapidly than the infection itself. The occurrence of super-spreader events leads to a critical threshold for the probability of spreading information, and only about 13% of initially informed individuals are necessary to result in widespread dissemination. The probability of causing a mem-epidemic is also expressed as a function of this threshold. The occurrence of large outbreaks can cause significant mortality rates, and the probability of a vaccine being safe but appearing symptomatic can cause misinformation to spread more rapidly than the infection itself. The model demonstrates that even a small increase in infection rates from one infected person to multiple others can cause misinformation to spread more rapidly than the infection itself.

This article collects key results concerning $C_0$-semigroups of operators on a complex topological vector space that exhibit codiskcyclicity or rapid codiskcyclicity. The content involves some novel findings and brings together established knowledge from the relevant literature. The primary focus is on the underlying dynamics of these semigroups, particularly concerning their generator's spectrum and cyclic behavior related to the closed unit disk in the spectrum.

We evaluate our recent coefficient method for assessing accuracy in estimating integrated magnetic flux from reconstructed vector magnetic fields. By testing the method on two synthetic datasets - one representing actual integrated magnetograms and another simulated data - we confirm its effectiveness in correctly representing integration errors as magnetic fill fraction varies. Furthermore, the method shows potential in providing a more precise estimation of magnetic field assessments by considering the magnetic fill fraction.

A new technique for three-dimensional photometry is utilized to investigate a vast sample of 747 young star clusters in the Milky Way, spanning masses from $10^6 M_\odot$. The study reveals a typical age-related decline in the clusters' central density, which can be explained by the age-dispersal timescale. The surface density of the clusters generally decreases with age, often fitting a typical Gr\"offenmann diagram, where the density decline is predicted to slow down after several hundred million years. The density distribution of the clusters generally conforms to a power-law profile, although the rate of decline varies significantly from one cluster to another. The surface density of the clusters is found to affect the mass of stars they produce and the probability of Type Ia supernovae occurrence in binary systems.

We tackle a major challenge in lattice QCD calculations of hadron decay widths, specifically three-particle decays, by introducing a newly computed finite-volume correction factor. This factor can be accurately applied to two-point correlation functions to determine the corresponding finite-volume decay widths. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach with a true three-particle system, namely $K^+ K^- e^+$, and also apply it to a pseudo-three-particle state, specifically the $B^+ B^0 e^-$ system.

We've developed inverse transforms made up of affine coupling layers with multiple values, which are highly efficient at inverting complicated functions that describe real physical systems. When combined with optimized sampling algorithms like Normalizing Flows, this results in a tool capable of creating joint distributions capable of efficiently answering questions about joint and conditional probabilities, while maintaining the ability to invert complex functions of physical relevance multiple times faster and with fewer resources than real-valued alternatives, particularly when applying to high-dimensional datasets.

This paper provides specific growth rates for the count of $y$-friable integers up to $x$ with a given size. A asymptotic formula, whose derivation relies heavily on smooth approximations of the step function and an accurate estimate for the Liouville function's partial sums, is derived for $\rho(\frac{\text{log } x}{\text{log } y})$. If the Random Walk Model (RWM) for the integers is correct, then the usual assumptions made in Friable Integer Theories - namely the independence, randomness and weak dependence of integers - will lead to the same predictions as the RWM. It also shows that under the hypothesis (RH) the RWM would give the same count as YFI Theory. A set of formulas, which could be used to compute $\rho(\frac{\text{log } x}{\text{log } y})$ for a wide range of values for $x$ and $y$, along with the associated error terms, is also derived.

Consider a subshift defined over a finite set of symbols with a non-zero topological entropy. When a non-degenerate morphism is applied to this subshift, the resulting image has the same topological entropy as the original subshift, provided the symbols have comparable sizes. This comparison of symbol sizes is modeled using a matrix, and the condition for comparison is referred to as the "recognizable" property. A significant consequence of this finding is that the topological entropy of the Raulf group, which is based on a 5-letter Dyck 2 code, is 2.
The retraining technique amplifies a language model's learning capacity from new data without encountering negative transfer in an unsupervised environment.

This paper introduces a novel kernel-based function, the m-ar-K function, which can be seen as an integrated version of ar-K functions, offering enhanced dimensionality reduction capabilities compared to existing ar-K methods. We demonstrate how the m-ar-K function can be applied to obtain a robust K-nearest neighbor classifier and show its performance efficiency via experimental results.

Our work provides a structured approach to identifying requirements in video games through a prioritized framework. As this framework begins to fill in the details, we see value in exploring several research paths ahead. These include adapting the framework for non-game interactive systems, integrating subjective user preferences into the model, and expanding data sources to include user feedback and developer discussions online.

An important aspect of machine learning model development involves the tuning of model hyperparameters through the evaluation of performance on validation datasets. While techniques like grid search are commonly employed for this purpose, researchers from Stanford and UK have created an innovative approach using continuous Heterogeneous Exchange Gradients (hXG) that enables simultaneous dataset partitioning and automatic grid search execution. Unlike conventional methods, their novel approach enables hyperparameter optimization using private validation datasets that are never shared, summed, or exposed to servers during peer-to-peer communication.

For any finite set of spheres in a pure dimension within the rational vector R^n, where the intersection points have only non-negative values, the arrangement generates a unique finite set of spheres with the same rational vector. This arrangement can be represented as the boundary of a specific arrangement of non-negative values in the rational vector space R^n. The ratio between the number of spheres in the arrangement and the number of spheres in its reduced form is equal to the ratio between the respective integers within the Coxeter group. The paper proves that this ratio is at least one and shows that the arrangement in the rational vector space serves as a generating set for the Coxeter group. Additionally, the rational vector's integers are not affected by subsequent reductions made by its own integer-subgroups. This result was initially shown for the arrangement in the rational vector space where the values are strictly positive, as long as the values are not zero. The proof involves one example to show that the integers within the Coxeter group are not dependent on the specific values within the rational vector space with the same positive-zero rational vector. The proof involves the Lemmas of R. Brauer and the arrangement of hyperplanes within the rational vector space. The ratio between the integers within the Coxeter group are equal to the ratio between the respective Hecke-algebras within the rational vector space. The ratio between the modules within the Coxeter group are equal to the ratio between the respective modules within the Hecke-algebras within the rational vector space.

We present an enhanced method for calculating the optimal filter under conditions of correlated noise, which is applicable to existing algorithms like those used in DECIGO or BBO. Our proposed approach refines the standard quasi-optimal weighting technique, providing a precise computation of the full coherent noise response curve, even in cases where the digital resampling introduces complex, potentially unpredictable noise patterns. This new approach is also capable of accounting for channel formation, dummy data generation, and sampling in a unified manner. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we simulated dummy data based on known signal inputs and applied our algorithm, showing its ability to accurately recover the signal with minimal error across the given frequency ranges.

While the study of chemically distinct stars has been extensively residual
abundance analysis is not routinely a focus in such research. This work presents
a comprehensive set of residual abundance data for approximately 800 stars from the
APOGEE-1 and APOGEE-2 datasets obtained at the 2.5m Katzman
Irwin--Falkoff Telescopes located at the W. M. Keck Observatory. The residual
abundances for 53 chemical elements were calculated using the SPECKTRUM
software and are openly accessible via an APOGEE specific page on the NOVA
website which also facilitates their exploration using interactive tools such as
Datashader and Bokeh as well as via machine-readable formats like ASCII tables
and FITS files. To ensure user-friendliness a tailored web interface along with
Python modules for interactive plotting of the data have been supplied. The
specktrum.apres package enables users to generate interactive residual abundance
plots from the dataset. Furthermore to aid in understanding the data the authors
have created a dataset of particularly distinctive stars exhibiting unusual
chemical compositions or kinematic properties. This subset is designed to
highlight the potential for identifying and studying unique stars and populations
using the publicly available APOGEE data. To create this subset each star was
assigned a score of uniqueness and is ranked in the resulting table along with
its score. The data described in this paper are the

This study analyzes early signals within the rumor propagation model on social networks, examining how they can offer insights into future dissemination patterns. Using a high school student network and a mobile application for data collection, we examined various factors that influence peak and attenuating phases of rumor propagation. Our analysis revealed that specific characteristics and geographical locations present before the peak stage can accurately forecast the peak and subsequent attenuation phases. As a result, we developed a theoretical model explaining the relationship between precursor features and peak/attenuation phases, as well as an empirical verification of this model's reliability. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of rumor propagation patterns on social networks.

Using the Hubble Space Telescope, we collected a planetary nebulae sample in the direction of the Fornax cluster, which consists of 37 PNe associated with eight host galaxies. Our findings include a positive distance excess for the Fornax cluster, with an average extra distance of 2.33±0.37 $h^{-1}$ Mpc when calculated using the planetary nebulae luminosity function, and 1.91±0.39 $h^{-1}$ Mpc when calculated using the shell expansion method, both results assuming CMB rest frame velocities. Our sample also enables us to study the nebular abundance of elements such as O, Ne, Mg, Si, and +-. We report a metallicity of -0.14±0.04 dex for the Fornax cluster, which is slightly lower than expected, and we also discuss the occurrence of enhanced abundances in some individual planetary nebulae.

We introduce LifeStream, an high-performance analytical engine for real-time data stream aggregation, which has been open-sourced on GitHub.  Unlike conventional approaches that employ optimized numerical libraries for bulk operations, LifeStream surpasses their performance when working with real-world datasets.  It achieves a significant speedup of up to 3.5x in complex stream queries.  Our research demonstrates the feasibility of handling multiple terabytes of data per day with real-world workloads, highlighting a 2.5x overall performance gain for typical queries.

This research extends the study of Bertrand curves by examining them in Finsler space, Cayley-Kahler space, and Sasakian space. It provides clear criteria for when a Bertrand curve is considered definite within these specific space types. Additionally, it offers methods to identify curves that fulfill the criteria for having a Bertrand counterpart in these particular space settings.

To examine how varying loss function combinations affect model performance, under-represented options such as KL Divergence were assessed. Our analysis revealed that contrary to expectations, a standalone KL Divergence loss yields nearly the same result as it does when used in addition to another loss function. This suggests that KL Divergence should be considered as a viable option on its own, rather than relying solely on its combination with other optimization functions.

This research paper investigates the impact of a boundary feedback loop, which is angle-dependent, on the control systems named 'Stokes' and 'Navier-Stokes'. The domain in question is a half-plane, restricted by a solid wall. We demonstrate the existence of stable solutions triggered by the feedback, as well as feedback-induced unstable solutions in both systems 'Stokes' and 'Navier-Stokes'. Furthermore, the study also delves into scenarios where time-varying feedback leads to solutions that grow exponentially in size.

This paper addresses strain-induced crystallization in polymers by applying statistical mechanics and thermodynamics to develop constitutive models. We focus on free energy and dissipation principles, utilizing network theory to describe molecular configurations and predict material behavior under various loading conditions and temperatures. Two modeling approaches are presented, involving distinct entropy formulas derived from configurational network theory and thermodynamics. These models are validated through experimental data for natural rubber under different temperatures and loading rates, revealing significant variations in crystalline and amorphous phase fractions. A phase diagram is generated to illustrate coexisting crystalline and amorphous phases under different loading rates and temperatures.

A detailed investigation into the interplay between unconventional superconductivity and topological properties of a Fermi surface is carried out using a microscopic BCS model. Specifically, the impact of a spherical Fermi surface on the symmetry, gap function and magnetic susceptibility of the superconducting state is analyzed. An analytical approach is employed to examine various types of interactions, resulting in findings that an anomalous behavior in the magnetic susceptibility occurs for both conventional and unconventional pairings near the Fermi surface surface, providing a characteristic indicator for the latter. Additionally, our results show that the more anomalous behavior in the microscopic gap determines the most prevalent symmetry in the microscopic superconducting gap. A study into the case of an anisotropic interaction reveals that this influences the magnetic susceptibility in the same way and also determines the behavior in the presence of a finite density of states.

The recent advancements in deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success, yet their intricate nature makes troubleshooting and performance enhancement challenging. To facilitate learning from experienced users, including instructors, in a range of typical tasks, we introduce a novel, interactive method for delivering targeted feedback through a chat interface. This interface enables the automatic generation of specific, directed feedback from instructors to learners, an approach that yields significant performance improvements, as demonstrated by our system outperforming a comparable baseline by 5.3% in accuracy after just two task demonstration-an outcome that is TDLR recommended.

A new decision-feedback algorithm for coherent detection of continuous-phase modulation (CPM) signals is proposed, achieving superior performance compared to conventional differential detection. The algorithm incorporates decision-feedback to recover the CPM signal's phase and employs multiple demodulators with distinct memory depths to break the inherent even floor in error rate found in differential detection. By selecting the demodulator output with the lowest error rate at each symbol interval, only a marginal loss in signal-to-noise ratio is found in total error rate. For instance, at a 10^-2 error rate, the proposed method yields a lower floor than conventional differential detection without requiring an additional signal-to-noise ratio, by utilizing a second demodulator with a different memory depth.

A gravitational wave event involving the merger of a black hole and a neutron star may go undetected if the neutron star is swallowed whole by the black hole, preventing the emission of an observable electromagnetic signal. To determine the radius of neutron-star event horizons that result in silent mergers, we established a relation based on the final mass of the resulting black hole. By employing three distinct populations of neutron stars and merging them with black holes of various radii, we identified precise thresholds: below these thresholds, a neutron star is entirely consumed, often leaving no observable evidence of the neutron star's existence. Above these thresholds, at least some mass of the neutron star is ejected, increasing the likelihood of a detectable electromagnetic signal. Our study indicates that for typical neutron-star equations of state, approximately 40% of such events would leave no trace, with larger black holes having a higher probability of silent mergers.

A key criterion for justifying the use of grand canonical ensemble simulations under constant pressure conditions is the rapid decline of compressibility as the system's size increases. We find that for a model system, a significant drop in compressibility is achievable without modifying the model. This objective can also be met by incorporating an artificial interaction between the ensemble and a heat bath simulated through a finite number of degrees of freedom. Consequently, we can achieve constant pressure grand canonical ensemble simulations via the canonical ensemble, given that the system's compressibility is inherently limited.

Existing rain generation datasets for training rain removal models have notable flaws, primarily induced labels and rain generation models that lack bidirectional consistency between rain generation and removal. This research proposes a novel approach to rain dataset creation with this duality in mind. The proposed Rain Generation Priors and Inpainting Network (RGIN) model uses priors and inpainting techniques to ensure bidirectional consistency. Evaluation metrics including SSIM, rain pixel detection accuracy, and model inference speed confirm RGIN's superiority over current models. When used as a rain dataset generator, RGIN also demonstrates exceptional performance in rain removal model training, especially with deep networks.

This document outlines a proposed method to accelerate human feedback processes in reward learning from batched comparisons. By leveraging a parallel processing system, this system can simultaneously evaluate multiple pairs of items, leading to concurrent assessments through an arbitrary function $f$. The proposed acceleration is based on the observation that similar items within batches enable the sharing of $f$'s computations, effectively making human feedback roughly $2\times$ faster when using $2\times$ as many samples. This technique is applicable to specific cases, prime number discovery, and general scenarios. The proposed method outperforms traditional approaches in terms of efficiency, evidenced by substantial reductions in computation time and cost per sample.

We investigate the impact of formalizing systematics in set theory on completeness properties in the context of model theory. By examining the variables affecting model companionship in a theory $T$, we focus on the significance of the signature used for axiomatic definition in set theory. Our research shows that, depending on the signature, the class of models for which model companionship is achievable varies. Ultimately, we identify two specific signatures, along with the necessary conditions, in which model companionship is preserved without restriction.

This research paper investigates the geometry of a specific type of a curved boundary condition, specifically a novel fractional version of a curvature related to the Bochner formula. It achieves convergence of an associated curvature flow under a particular sigma-stabilized fractional heat equation definition and proves the existence of a fixed-point solution to the equation's initial value problem.

A comprehensive database of drug-related incidents in the USA from 1990 to 2017, compiled by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, enabled us to analyze the absorption of ten major psychoactive drugs. We employed a modified version of the Kuhn-Tucker conditions to investigate consumption patterns, considering price, availability, and demographic factors. Our study revealed that consumption of certain drugs followed similar trends, with seven of them exhibiting correlated changes in intake. Specifically, seven drugs including marijuana, prescription opioids, cocaine, phentermine, ecstasy, methamphetamines, and LSD showed correlated consumption patterns. Moreover, we observed that the absorption of these drugs declined over time, with their half lives ranging from one to three years. However, illicit drugs with alternative forms or a less significant impact demonstrated half lives exceeding five years.

Among the most pivotal advancements in neural language models is their capacity to learn the inherent connections between words. Prior studies have successfully demonstrated that utilizing pre-annotated dependencies can significantly enhance the models' performance on various natural language processing tasks. However, the majority of these studies focus on the use of tree-like structures, while less exploration has been done on capturing the complex web of linguistic relations that are not confined to a tree structure. To address this limitation, our study's main findings show that neural models' ability to understand and apply non-tree-like linguistic relations can be substantially improved, with a notable 4\% increase in accuracy on the NLI task achieved through the use of if-then relation data. Notably, the results indicate that a non-linear training approach outperforms traditional tree-based methods by about 1\%, while the inclusion of if-then data leads to a substantial 10\% performance boost\,.

As intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processors become operational, the feasibility of implementing the HHL algorithm in a NISQ-friendly version and executing it on these processors is being explored. An approximate version of the original HHL algorithm has been proposed, specifically designed for PEA-based methods. This new proposal, called HHL-AP2, replaces traditional amplitude encodings with 2D quantum circuits featuring applied layer structures. By incorporating the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) into HHL-AP2 and leveraging the sparsity of H's inverse, the algorithm achieves significant reductions in required qubits and classical measurements, thereby improving the efficiency of SPARROW-HHL. When put to the test on a real-world quantum processor from IBM's London iQX system, HLL-AP2 successfully emulated the action of H's inverse using just 9 qubits and 25 classical measurement shots per result.

This paper introduces a novel technique, bidirectional attention (BiAM), to strengthen the connection between speech representations and linguistic information in the transcription area of subword units in an end-to-end automated speech recognition system. By applying the BiAM module twice in the training process with different target units (speech and linguistic information) and attention sources (linguistic and speech representations), the BiAM can learn the optimal alignment between them. For both Yau's conformal Menger curvature and White's area gauge curvature, stationary forms can be characterized in three-dimensional space. Likewise, this characterization holds in eight-dimensional space when considering the special curvature defined in both the AR and SW variants.

This study examines an ergodic Markov chain consisting of random parkings on the integers, where each integer has a associated value of zero or one, and the values at consecutive integers are also paired. The values are randomly reconfigured according to the rules of sequential parking, with the sequence shifting one position to the left after each parking. We make a key observation: as the parking sequence length (denoted by n) grows, we can expect the first k_n parking places (where k_n also grows) to reflect a hypergeometric distribution. This holds true whether measuring similarity through total variation distance or Kolmogorov distance, with both being quantified relative to n and k_n.

Researchers have conducted an in-depth study on a hybrid circuit featuring two Josephson junctions within superconducting nanowires. The unique configuration allows for modulation of a critical voltage threshold through the application of an electric current. Below this threshold, coherent quantum states of the circuit's charge and momentum are sustained. The threshold can be systematically altered by adjusting the system's parameters, and the researchers observed that shifting it leads to corresponding alterations in the threshold's slope. The study provides theoretical calculations supported by experimental data and numerical simulations, revealing that the threshold depends on the relative orientation of gate voltages applied to the Josephson junctions. Furthermore, the researchers have identified opportunities to decouple the circuit's charge and momentum states by manipulating the system's parameters, and adjusted the threshold to zero resulting in an equal superposition of opposite momentum states.

GJ 229B, an intermediate brown dwarf or large planetary object, has a distinct atmosphere.  By utilizing an advanced computer model of its atmosphere, researchers have accurately predicted its characteristics and found evidence of a possible dinosaur-sized meteor on its surface.  This discovery has actual implications, as the detection of this meteor could be possible with a space telescope.  Furthermore, comparing observations of GJ 229B with the computer model has provided insight into its formation process.  This process has left an indelible mark on GJ 229B's atmosphere's characteristics and composition.  Specifically, evidence points towards the meteor shedding hydrocarbons and water vapor that are now observable with the James Webb Space Telescope.  In addition, there is likely to be remnants of the giant planets that formed around GJ 229B by accretting GJ 229B's hydrogen vapor, which could also be detectable with the space telescope.  This discovery has a significant impact on our understanding of the relationship between the formation of brown dwarfs, planets, and satellites.

Researchers have derived the PDF for a quark plasma without interactions, denoted as $f(x,iP_{\perp}^{2},T)$, in both longitudinal and transverse variations, provided that the S-Matrix has a diagonal form. Utilizing this definition, they have determined the T-dependent PDF parameters $x$ and $P_{\perp}$ for non-interacting quarks. Furthermore, parton recombination within the hadron have been discussed in the context of the factorization formula.

Building on successful strategies to predict videos from unseen viewpoints, our building block building block is a dual representation framework combining global scene descriptors and local image components. By leveraging this framework, we can accurately predict videos from unseen viewpoints. This is achieved by decomposing images into viewpoint-independent components and encoding them using a neural network. This results in a dual representation framework where the global descriptor captures the scene's overall structure, while a neural network predictor encodes the descriptor and viewer-centered retinal information to generate accurate predictions. By decoupling view-dependent and view-independent features in this network, our model is able to prevent overfitting and outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in prediction quality and speed. By tuning only the encoder for real-time applications, our framework outperforms previous techniques in prediction quality and speed. By using this framework, our model is able to accurately predict videos from unseen viewpoints.

A photon-based circuit component called a beam splitter divides a photon's wavefunction into different modes. To build more sophisticated devices like photonic quantum processors, this component should access multiple modes of light. A simple and efficient way to create beam splitters in basic circuits is by coupling a waveguide to a resonator. However, in reality, this process introduces only a small amount of higher-order photonic modes. Here, we theoretically design a beam splitter capable of equalizing a large number of modes by calculating the necessary dimensions for this component. A practical demonstration of this design was achieved by building a beam splitter on a sample and observing that it indeed activates the expected modes, which were then further validated by measuring a photon quantum gate.

Using a potential model with a complex function, we've calculated and studied the mass spectra of certain baryon states that decay rapidly. Our calculations are supported by experimental data for some two-quark resonances, while also indicating the possibility of "hidden" exotica within the spectrum. Our study highlights that the complexity of the quark's potential might give rise to these exotic states.

An ongoing investigation seeks to assess the effectiveness of predicting airborne particle distribution in indoor spaces infected with COVID-19. Various well-mixed and complex models were employed to conduct this prediction using open-source tools related to airflow and aerosol transport. These tools were also used to simulate the concentration of airborne particles around an individual who has been coughing in a room. The results showed that even with its simplicity, the well-mixed model accurately forecasts the average concentration of aerosols around the coughing patient when compared to more intricate models. The research also highlights the limitations of well-mixed models in predicting spatial distribution patterns of particles. To overcome this, the investigators developed a more advanced computational model incorporating realistic airflow and particle transport. The findings from this study are available for replication using open-source codes, which facilitate the exploration of multiple scenarios. These codes and initial replication data are freely accessible online.

Quantum vacuum diffraction and birefringence arise from the interaction between curved spacetime and quantized electromagnetic fields, with their effects influenced by the direction of x-ray propagation relative to the gravito-inertial field. This phenomenon can result in either an additive or subtractive combination of these effects, potentially yielding entirely new manifestations. Notably, this interaction can cause vacuum birefringence to override vacuum diffraction, causing beam shifts in the direction of Gravitational Lens effect. To achieve this manifestation, it requires placing a block of magnetized material at a specific distance from the x-ray source, with the required distance determined by the frequency of the x-ray photons and the strength of the local gravitational field. Such conditions can be met on board an astrophysical satellite or in a location with extremely strong gravity, such as near a black hole. This could potentially allow for the verification of vacuum beam shifts in such environments.

We developed an algorithm to construct fully transitive polyhedra in n-dimensional space, with the capability to execute specific constructions in n-1 dimensions based on a given polyhedron in n-dimensions, derived from the comm relations of a birecurrent Baum-Sertner group in 3-dimensions.

A primary objective in copy-protection research is developing practical methods to safeguard copyrighted material from unauthorized duplication. Traditionally, copy-protection schemes relied on trusted parties to distribute secret keys for authorized access by legitimate users. Recently, some notable advancements emerged in copy-protection unlearnable functions and related areas without relying on trusted parties. In this research, we investigate unclonable encryption as a standalone concept, examining its feasibility to protect copyrighted digital content from unauthorized duplication through secure decryption by authorized users as its fundamental goal. Initially, we demonstrate the impossibility of unclonable encryption for general functions due to an attack exploiting the ability to combine multiple copies into a single copy. However, we propose a public-key unclonable encryption scheme for specific functions evaluable with short circuits, achieving perfect security against attacks involving any polynomial number of copies. Furthermore, we examine key-switchable unclonable encryption and discover that the previously described schemes achieve this with attacks limiting themselves to copying any small number of times.

A modified version of a code used in a channel, where an observer attempts to detect if a user has been impersonated, is examined. Research shows that there's a specific threshold for the coding rate - both above and below which, there's a different way to adjust the error probabilities for detection and impersonation. As the coding rate approaches threshold, the probabilities converge to related values. Furthermore, altering the modified code to another specific version results in an increase in error probabilities for observation and impersonation.

A twisted bilayer MoS2 placed on a SiO2 substrate was studied using a combined experimental and theoretical approach to analyze its electronic properties.  In a combined experiment, aartugel MoS2 placed on top of a silicon dioxide surface exhibited a broad plasmon at an energy of 0.4 eV.  In contrast, DFT calculations showed higher plasmon energies in suspended and free-standing MoS2 layers, at 2.85 eV and 2.95 e respective.  Both values decreased with relaxation of the MoS2 lattice, dropping to 2.77 eV and 2.65 eV.  A charge transfer from MoS2 to SiO2 further lowered the plasmon energy to 2.59 eV.  In contrast, strain did not have a significant effect on the plasmon energy.  Increasing the doping level increased the plasmon energy in both suspended and charge-transferred models.  Notably, a specific doping level of approximately 0.05 electrons per unit cell resulted in a plasmon energy of approximately 2.65 eV, which was 1 eV higher than the plasmon energy observed in the experimental setup.  This value was within a measurable range and could be accessed with a suitable plasmon generator.

This paper presents precise criteria to classify almost conformal Ricci solitons as almost conformal gradient Ricci solitons. It also provides related characterizations and examines specific examples on certain spaces, including the Heisenberg group and the metric product of the real line and a circle.

Plasma physics within stellar and planetary magnetospheres, shaped by their respective winds, exhibits significant similarities and differences, often leading to the extrapolation of planetary processes to stellar counterparts. This review statement of purpose, will use these processes to set the stage for in-depth investigations of magnetospheric phenomena in both domains.

We've created multiple layers of nanometric Bi and Co to study the interaction between Bi's interlayer spacing and Co's magnetic properties. X-ray scattering data shows the presence of distinct Bi layers as well as significant layer thickness dependence of the electron density within the layers. This led to the discovery of a new, by now dominant, scattering mechanism within the Hall effect that's directly correlated with the mean interlayer distance of the Bi. This effect is capable of modifying or even overriding the Hall effect contributed by the magnetization of the Co's within the multilayer structure. Additionally, we observed a shift in the onset of Bi's ferromagnetic alignment relative to the Co's as a result of increased electron density within the Bi's, and this relative alignment data could be used to determine the mean magnetic moment within the sample. Lastly, the anomalous Hall effect exhibited a non-monotonic behavior due to various Bi's factors and could be modified to display Bi's dominant contribution by adjusting the Co's layer thickness.

In a recent study of N-dimensional Schrödinger equations with a fractional potential, researchers analyzed two distinct cases: when 0 is less than or equal to $\alpha$ but strictly less than N, and when $\alpha$ is strictly greater than or equal to N. The first case led to a bounded, non-negative finite value, while the second case resulted in linear behavior for large values of $|x|$. The dispersion relation could be derived from the eigenvalue $\lambda_0$ in both scenarios. Additionally, a complete set of orthogonal eigenfunctions was identified, allowing for the representation of any square-integrable function in N-dimensional space.

This study examines how different p-norms (specifically Euclidean or $l_2$ and Manhattan or $l_1$) impact the final performance of neural networks trained using a specific optimization algorithm. This algorithm generates a neural network with a restricted Lipschitz constant under both p-norms. Our research theory posits that the choice of p-norm during training can significantly influence the generalization capabilities of the resulting neural network. To validate these assumptions, we conduct a series of rigorous numerical experiments using the chosen p-norm as a control variable in the training process, but evaluate the network's performance using the standard Euclidean norm. Our findings showcase the $l_1$-trained networks' exceptional ability to outperform $l_2$-trained networks under certain conditions, thus demonstrating the importance of p-norm selection in shaping a neural network's effectiveness.

Human comprehension and production of language are guided by the sentence structure's simultaneous linear and hierarchical components.
Current deep learning-based language models, however, are primarily sequential, effectively capturing only the linear aspects of sentences.
While their general performance is impressive, their success depends on the specific sentence features they implicitly encode during training.
One key question is whether there exists a universal, step-by-step method for understanding sentences that successfully addresses both linear and hierarchical components.
Such a method would enable the development of learning agents with sentence structure awareness.
We conducted a series of experiments on sequential parsers, including the cyclic bank parser, to determine if any describe a universal procedure for analyzing sentences.
Our results indicate that no such procedure exists; instead, the successful parsers encode sentence grammar properties implicitly.
Due to the lack of explicit encoding, the parsing rules are inapplicable to unseen sentences.
We propose that implicit encoding arises from the disparity between the procedure's output and the target representation.
Our empirical evidence suggests that minimizing this discrepancy during training leads to implicit encoding of sentence grammar properties.

Researchers analyzed the far-ultraviolet and soft X-ray/UV radiation from the star HD 806063, witnessing its transition from an EV I to an F0/VI star. The subsequent stellar flux was used to calculate the temperature and radiative temperatures of HD 80606b as the planet moved through different parts of its orbit. The effective temperature of HD 80606b dropped below 1000K at the L4/L5 points during this stage of its orbit. Stellar radiation caused the planet's dayside temperature to rise above 1200K just before it passed behind its host star. A detailed model of the planet's atmosphere was created to predict the atmospheric composition, atmospheric structure, and wind patterns in a wide range of regions along its orbit. The results showed a significant amount of molecular hydrogen on the planet's dayside, as well as possible silicate clouds, while the nightside and transitional areas showed mostly atomic hydrogen, helium, and heavier elements like carbon, oxygen, and sodium. The analysis also showed that the atmospheric wind speeds could reach supersonic levels of up to 20km/s along the orbit, while horizontal wind speeds around the L4/L5 points were below 1000K. The analysis also showed that the horizontal winds around these points were relatively calm, while the radiative temperatures at these points were above 500K. Virtual coaches for exercises are becoming popular in the form of engaging, game-like experiences that motivate users through rewards and friendly competition. The underlying systems for these experiences rely heavily on tracking exercise performance, yet they require precise settings that strike a balance between making exercises feel rewarding without being too frustrating. We've developed an efficient, user-friendly tool to help designers test various approaches to tracking performance, aiming to improve the overall effectiveness of gamified exercise programs. Our tool, which can be run on everyday computers, involves extensive user studies to determine the best methods for tracking performance. As an open-source project licensed under MIT, our codebase can be freely used, studied, and redistributed, with attribution to the original authors.

This research compares the geometrically nonlinear elasticity and linearised elasticity frameworks in relation to brittle fracture energies, specifically examining $n$-th power and Saint-Venant-Kirchhoff models in high-energy limits as they converge to fractionalised linearised elasticity energies. It finds that for $n$-power theory, significant discrepancies arise in two-dimensional cases but vanish in one and three-dimensional scenarios. Conversely, the convergence of the $\Gamma$-limits yields the same results across all dimensions.

The Standard Model's lepton universality principle suggests that vector leptoquarks should produce identical first-generation and third-generation pair yields. Non-leptonic search strategies, which have limited background needs, are being utilized for an experimental LHC search. To improve signal representation in this study, a novel method incorporating next-to-leading order QCD corrections was implemented, and multiple signal normalisation parameters were employed. Following the analysis of $pp$ collision data at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeFS with 44.7 fb-1 of collected information, no significant deviation from expected background levels was found. As a result, the lepton universality assumption can be upheld with 95% confidence intervals, allowing for vector leptoquark exclusion up to mass thresholds of 1542, 1460, and 1369 GeV for the available scalar and tensor leptoquark parameter sets.

Researchers developed a supervised learning approach called a deep neural network (DNN) to enhance the quality of low-dose positron emission tomography (PET) images when combined with corresponding MRI data. This framework, specifically designed for the improvement of 21-cog PET/MRI scans with an 8-minute acquisition time, was trained using pairs of high-dose PET scans (21-minute acquisition time) and corresponding MRI data. Initially, the low-dose PET image underwent basic preprocessing steps including downscaling to 2.0 mm and a circular crop to match the high-dose PET field of view. Then, the improved DNN framework automatically learned to map the low-dose PET image to its high-dose PET image equivalent. By utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, the DNN first aligned the corresponding high-dose PET and MRI images through intensity normalization and Nn-convolutions followed by a batch normalization. This was aimed at countering the Down-sampling and Down-scaling effects. Next, the improved DNN framework counted the corresponding de-noising process. By employing a residual learning approach, the improved DNN framework achieved a significant improvement in low-dose PET image quality. The rise of artificial intelligence in information recommendation has enabled personalized news delivery. While this offers individual benefits, it also poses a threat to user privacy through data collection. Our survey of 581 participants, segmented by age, aims to explore the nuances of privacy concerns and personalization preferences in today's digitally connected world. The results reveal a complex dynamic where users value personalized news but are wary of privacy invasion, with age playing a significant role in shaping these views. Older individuals are less interested in personalized content and exhibit higher privacy concerns compared to younger groups. The research also uncovers a discrepancy between users' stated views and observed behaviors, with many engaging in privacy-related deceptive actions to secure personalization benefits. The study's findings offer valuable insights for developing personalized news systems that strike a balance between user preferences, privacy, and system efficacy.

Previous studies have shown that using contextual embeddings within neural networks for coreference prediction exceeds the basic principles of centering theory. However, it's been observed that these models don't fully capture the advanced principles of the PPOP extension of centering theory. This study investigates the relationship between neural coreference models and the PPOP extension, as well as exploring how these models can be enhanced to better represent the PPOP. Our findings reveal that the impact of contextualized embeddings on PPOOP principle prediction depends on the specific neural network architecture and configuration employed. Additionally, we found that incorporating configuration features directly into the neural coreference model enables it to surpass the PPOOP principle.

We present a new $2^{tw} \cdot n$-algorithm for finding a transitive edge in a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where edge labels are from a set of size $k$. This algorithm can be seen as an improvement to existing parameterized algorithms that depend on DAG treewidth. By combining it with other methods, we obtain a more efficient overall algorithm for DAGs. Additionally, we provide a parameterized algorithm for DAGs that runs in $k^{tw} \cdot n$ time. This side by side with the known exponential algorithm in treewidth for directed graphs lacking a transitive edge.

Using mathematical optimization to configure complex systems offers a significant advantage by distilling multiple system aspects into a singular objective: maximization. This strategy not only enhances human comprehension but also enhances performance on evaluation metrics. Building on this concept, we developed a innovative pipeline using optimization for parsing, simplifying, and enhancing models of human reasoning processes represented as first-order logic models. Through automated processing, we achieved a 4% improvement in the accuracy of these models, as measured by human performance on validation datasets.

To systematize studies of operator growth under time evolution within quantum many-body systems, we propose leveraging symmetry to drastically reduce complexity in calculations involving the K-complexity of unitary operators. By utilizing the commutation relations between a system's Hamiltonian and its symmetry generators, we develop general formulas for computing K-complexity, which also reveals an alternative, potentially more practical definition based on the expansion of Taylor series in parameter space. These defined quantities satisfy expected properties, such as time-derivative relations and upper bound inequalities. The conservation of total spin in the Transverse Field Ising Model serves as a framework to demonstrate our approach, where K-complexity, K-speed, and K-acceleration are explicitly calculated and found to be consistent with previous results by J. S. Rousohova using a different methodology.

In outdoor localization systems based on WiFi, signal strength measurements often lead to inaccurate location estimates due to the imprecise distance calculations between WiFi fingerprints in a heatmap. To address this issue, we leveraged the spatial correlation between adjacent signals to train machine learning models that could predict geospatial distances more effectively. Our evaluation, conducted in two distinct environments, revealed significant improvements in estimate accuracy using these models. Furthermore, incorporating this enhanced distance metric into a modified multilateration algorithm resulted in more precise location predictions, revealing a direct correlation between more accurate distance estimates and reduced localization errors.

To sustain electrical power needs, a Type II civilization on Earth would require approximately 10^21 Watts, an amount achievable by any type of energy source, including controlled thermonuclear fusion, solar power, nuclear fission, chemical energy, and even geothermal heat. However, if we consider more advanced options like dark matter annihilation, extra-dimensional gravity leaks, and N-type nucleobarns, only dark matter works as it could supply the necessary energy without overwhelming Earth's radiative output. By leveraging the constraints on the dark matter scattering cross-section with nuclei, we determine that this source is limited to around 10^21 Watts. In comparison, we calculate that nucleobarns could be controlled to provide the required energy, while we reject the feasibility of exploiting gravity or extra-dimensional phenomena for this purpose.

This paper proposes utilizing P2P technology to create flexible and cost-effective Service Level Agreement (SLA) guarantees for streaming media by enabling precise and cost-effective network performance monitoring. Traditionally, SLA definitions have been constrained to simple metrics like end-to-end latency and packet loss, neglecting the complexities of user experience which involve both objective and subjective aspects of media playback. To address this, a protocol is introduced that leverages P2P technology to facilitate media playback while satisfying medium fidelity requirements outlined in the SLA. This protocol utilizes peer contributions to a DHT structure to monitor different network paths and both objective and subjective playback experiences, enabling a media server to employ real-time P2P performance monitoring data to generate an encoding graph that ensures smooth media playback with minimal peer to peer interactions.

In the event of an energy recovery linac (ERL) utilizing multiple passes with various beam currents and fill patterns, changes in beam filling can lead to alterations in beam-RF interactions even within the same pass. A methodology has been developed to define the fill pattern energy recovery linac (ERL) choice that impacts beam-RF interactions and threshold current levels. Furthermore, modeling methods for beam-RF interactions in multiple-pass energy recovery linacs have been explored, with implications on transverse and longitudinal beam stability in various passes considered.

The primary goal of this research is to accurately determine the total neutron cross section within a scintillator material using a wide range of neutron energies (from 98 to 688 MeV). To achieve this, the experiment employs a two-stage approach, where the first stage measures the number of neutrons that exit the scintillator, and the second stage uses a proton scintillator to detect the interaction between neutrons and the target, thereby allowing for the calculation of the cross section. The results obtained from this two-stage approach, where the product of the two measured quantities is directly proportional to the cross section, show consistent outcomes across the entire energy range tested, with the degree of consistency falling within two standard deviations.

Cometary bodies like comets 67P and Churyumov-Gerasimenko contain remnants of early solar system building blocks, which we analyzed to uncover their formation history. By linking the high increase in sticking forces observed in super-dry samples to optimal temperatures (150-200 K) for planetesimal formation, we suggest a cooler environment (around 100 K) was prevalent closer to the sun. We modeled the evolution of this region, starting near the snow line, where temperatures gradually decreased to the required range. The model predicts that both small and large agglomerates, formed in this region, could survive and be transported to the outer solar system, where they were eventually shaped by gravitational forces. The surface properties of these chondrites match the albedo and thermal behavior of 67P, but distinguishing between this formation model and the traditional cold collapse model will require more detailed comparisons with other shapes and behaviors of cometary bodies.

examines the connections between three classification methods (Fisher's discriminant
analysis, sequential Fisher's discriminant analysis, and method of maximum likelihood)
and Factor Analysis by Sequential Mixtures (PASAM). Furthermore, the package's
internal workings are outlined, utilizing R, with its visualization capabilities
demonstrated through an example in the PASAM R package.

Robot skill learning often involves navigating a complex state-space while adhering to complex temporal safety guidelines.  Introducing the challenge of highly nonlinear, intricate constraints that are difficult to define mathematically.  We have identified real-world safety guidelines as a prime example of this problem.  Constrained imitation learning aims to resolve this issue by setting dynamic safety boundaries within state-space representations through physical boundaries.  To test this approach, we have developed an algorithm that can translate these physical constraints into mathematical formulations that are both efficient for online execution and robust, with no need to recompute safety controls based on the robot's exact dynamics.  Furthermore, we have developed methods for incorporating this transformed knowledge into model predictive control to ensure compliance with these constraints.  Through a variety of robotic skills, we have demonstrated the effectiveness of constrained imitation learning in achieving robust safety guideline learning in real-world applications.

To gain a deeper understanding, we recast the two-gluon form factor matrix element in QCD, specifically the six-gluon CEV form factor at one-loop level, previously computed by Del Duca, Melnikov, Vladimirov, and others. This involves the integral over the six-dimensional momentum space of the remaining four internal momenta. By leveraging the exceptional partial fractions identity in $ \text{N=4} $ super Yang-Mills theory, the relevant amplitudes can be simplified, thus reducing the problem to a linear algebraic equation system. This reformulated approach allows us to derive the hard limit of the six-gluon CEV form factor in $ \text{N=4} $ SYM at one-loop level in the collinear limit of external gluons 1 and 2, utilizing the IR anomalous dimension in $ \text{N=4} $ SYM and the finite part at one-loop level in a regularization scheme where the color dglap equation holds, specifically the DDM basis.
